---
title: "Installation"
---

MINTverse is two packages. `estimint` maps a measured prevalence to transmission
intensity, and `stateMINT` emulates the prevalence and case trajectories that follow an
intervention. Install both:

```bash
pip install estimint mintstate
```

The equivalent inside a project managed by [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) is:

```bash
uv add estimint mintstate
```

Python 3.12 or newer is required. Both packages declare it, and neither will install on
an older interpreter.

::: {.callout-note}
## Distribution name and import name

`stateMINT` is published on PyPI as **`mintstate`**, so you install `mintstate` and you
import `stateMINT`:

```python
import stateMINT          # correct
import mintstate          # ModuleNotFoundError
```

`estimint` has no such split. The distribution and the module are both `estimint`.
:::

## Extras

An extra is an optional set of dependencies, named in square brackets after the package.
`estimint` on its own gives you the EIR and HBR models and no emulator, so without
`mintstate` alongside it there are no trajectories. The rest of the extras are only
needed for refitting the models, for the bundled plotting helpers, or for a GPU.

| Extra | Command | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `scenarios` | `pip install "estimint[scenarios]"` | `mintstate`, the same result as naming it yourself. |
| `viz` | `pip install "estimint[viz]"` | matplotlib, for the bundled plotting helpers. |
| `download` | `pip install "estimint[download]"` | The fetchers used to pull training data. |
| `train` | `pip install "estimint[train]"` | duckdb, scikit-learn and pyarrow, for refitting the XGBoost models. |
| `all` | `pip install "estimint[all]"` | The four `estimint` extras above. |
| `gpu` | `pip install "mintstate[gpu]"` | `jax[cuda12]`, so the emulator runs on an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12. |

A GPU is optional. The CPU build of JAX, which the emulator runs on, is fast enough for
inference, where a ten-scenario batch takes about a second, and the `gpu` extra is only
needed if you are training or sweeping a grid of thousands.

## Model weights

`estimint` ships its three XGBoost models (prevalence, HBR and EIR-to-HBR) inside the
wheel, so `load_xgb_model("prevalence")` reads a file that is already on disk and never
needs a network.

`stateMINT` does need one on first use, because its checkpoints live in the Hugging Face
repository [`dide-ic/stateMINT`](https://huggingface.co/dide-ic/stateMINT), with a
separately trained checkpoint of about 38 MB for each predictor under `prevalence/` and
`cases/`. The first call that needs one fetches it and caches it under
`~/.cache/huggingface`, and every later call reads the cache. The first `run_scenarios`
of a new install is therefore slower than all the ones that follow it. Warm both caches up
front so that the download does not interrupt a session. `preload_models()` loads the
XGBoost models and pulls the stateMINT weights.

```python
from estimint import preload_models

preload_models()
```

## Working offline

On a cluster node or an air-gapped machine, warm the cache somewhere with a network
first, then set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` so that Hugging Face never attempts a request and
resolves everything from `~/.cache/huggingface`:

```bash
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
```

If the cache directory itself is unavailable, put the weights somewhere you control and
load them from a path, since `from_pretrained` takes a `local_dir` and will read a
directory laid out like the repository instead of calling the Hub.

```python
from stateMINT.model import Mamba2Regressor

artifact = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained(
    "dide-ic/stateMINT",
    predictor="prevalence",
    revision="v1.2.2",
    local_dir="/shared/models/stateMINT",
)
```

## Verify the install

`importlib.metadata` reports the version of an installed distribution rather than of an
imported module, so the emulator's version is recorded under `mintstate` and not under
`stateMINT`. `net_types()` asks `estimint` which net formulations it knows about.

```{python}
import importlib.metadata as md

import estimint
import stateMINT

print("estimint  (import estimint) ", md.version("estimint"))
print("mintstate (import stateMINT)", md.version("mintstate"))
print()
print("net types:", estimint.net_types())
```

Four net formulations and no error confirms that both packages are installed correctly.
